title: Can a small validation leaderboard rank robustness predictors? Identifiability limits in AIMO-Interp
TLDR: On the frozen AIMO-Interp validation snapshot, only perfect-score owners survive selection plus BH; sustained single-rule power needs 76 or 169 independent items at the stated effects.
abstract: On the frozen AIMO-Interp public validation board (14 Small and 21 Main items, inferred from the score grid), no score below perfect is separable from the independent fair-coin null after per-owner selection and across-owner Benjamini–Hochberg correction: 59 of 61 Small owners and 40 of 41 Main owners are not rejected, including an owner with a 12/14 Small result. The snapshot predates the organizers' 21 October removal of two perfect-score submissions attributed to iterative profiling of problems and labels. We do not identify which owners were affected. [S13] Our hash-pinned analysis adjusts each owner's best visible score for its number of scored submissions under an independent-submission model. Only perfect observed owner results reject the declared null; non-rejection leaves chance performance, method equivalence and pairwise ranking unresolved. A single pre-specified predictor needs at least 76 independent correctness items at true accuracy 0.65, or 169 at 0.6, to sustain power 0.8 at level 0.05 before selection correction. We offer this as a design target for future validation boards, not as a statement about the unpublished final set. Paired, problem-clustered method comparisons need separate sizing. A supporting public-label audit finds no mixed labels among 11 Small problems with multiple checkpoints. We provide CPU reproduction and frozen reference baselines whose private-validation results remain unmeasured.
